title: Handoff Artifacts
description: Typed handoff contracts between workflow stages. Each stage with a `produces` field writes .work-state/artifacts/<id>.json matching the schema below. Downstream stages declare these ids in `consumes` and read them from disk instead of receiving pasted prose. Artifacts survive context compaction and make the inter-stage contract explicit. Native readable specification

answers.description: User answers (interactive) or auto-resolved defaults with rationale (autonomous).

chosen.description: Option id chosen by user (interactive) or option #1 (autonomous).

api_contract.description: DTOs/endpoints shared by backend+frontend in full-stack tasks.

build_status.description: Worker-reported check status only; independent qa_tests is the workflow QA authority.

worker_attested.description: Optional worker self-attestation; never substitutes for the independent qa_tests artifact.

scope.description: Project-defined scope names touched (e.g. backend-kotlin, go, frontend, mobile, devops, rust). Matches scope_map in team.config.

conformance_evidence.description: Canonical typed evidence envelope. CTO conformance reads only entries persisted in this artifact; caller wrappers may select an entry but cannot author its semantics.

quality_gate_evidence.description: Canonical typed quality-gate envelope. CTO conformance derives gate status from persisted gates, never from caller wrappers.

verdict.description: Normalized overall verdict, derived DETERMINISTICALLY from findings (not eyeballed): `reject` if any unresolved CRITICAL finding; else `needs_changes` if any HIGH or MEDIUM; else `approve`. The review stage gate keys on this (`verdict != reject`) instead of a subjective 'confidence>=80'. An unknown/missing verdict blocks closure — it never auto-approves.

zone.description: Project-defined scope name (e.g. backend-kotlin, go, frontend, mobile, devops, rust) matching a scope_map entry. Used to route the Phase 6.5 fix to the right developer role.

findings.description: Only findings with confidence >= 80 are recorded.

manual_qa.description: Manual runtime-verification verdict, produced by the manual-qa agent AFTER review_fixes — it exercises the code that will actually ship, not a pre-fix snapshot. NOT UI-only: on a UI scope it drives the real UI through OMP browser or configured device automation; on a backend/CLI scope it runs the app, hits endpoints, and reads logs/output. Gated on scope.has_runtime (skipped only for pure docs/config work). PASS requires every acceptance criterion to be observed at runtime. CONDITIONAL is terminal only when deterministic/runtime checks produced real evidence but one or more required criteria are unavailable because an explicit capability, credential, or configuration blocker is recorded in blocked_prerequisites. FAIL means an observed failure. Missing or unknown verdicts fail closed. Consumed by qa_tests (evidence → automated regression tests) and by summary. Replaces the old string field inside `debug`.

verdict.description: PASS only if every acceptance criterion was observed working at runtime. CONDITIONAL only when deterministic/runtime checks produced real evidence but a required criterion is unobservable because an explicit capability, credential, or configuration blocker is recorded in blocked_prerequisites. FAIL means an observed failure. A missing/unknown verdict is treated as FAIL — it never auto-passes.

evidence.description: At least one concrete observation is required for every terminal verdict. UI: screenshot path + WHAT IS VISIBLE on it. Backend/CLI: the command/curl run + the actual response/exit code, and the relevant log lines. A bare 'looks good' is not evidence.

mode.description: Which verification mode was used: 'ui' (OMP browser for web or configured device automation for the app) when scope.has_ui, else 'runtime' (run/curl/logs).

dod_additions.description: UI/visual acceptance criteria manual-qa appends back to dod.json (see multi-source DoD fan-in). Each item uses the dod item shape.

regressions.description: Pre-existing behavior that broke during testing — empty array if none.

blocked_prerequisites.description: Optional explicit capability, credential, or configuration blockers that make required acceptance criteria unobservable. Required evidence for a CONDITIONAL verdict: identify the unavailable criterion and the blocker without including secrets, raw provider/media data, or fabricated positive live evidence.

qa_tests.description: Independent automated QA report produced after implementation and review-fixes. The workflow gate reads only this canonical artifact's build_status; implementation/review-fix/manual-QA reports are informational worker attestations and never substitute for it.

based_on_manual_qa.description: true when the tests encode manual_qa observations (has_ui path).

feature_spec.description: Optional slim feature specification — 8 sections distilled from a 15-section template. The discovery stage of a FEATURE workflow MAY produce it when the task warrants a written contract; it is not mandatory. Consumed by architecture and by manual-qa (acceptance_criteria becomes the manual test checklist). Gate-able via feature_spec_present when a project wants to require it.

goal.description: One-paragraph statement of what and why.

anti_scope.description: Explicitly out of scope — the boundary.

acceptance_criteria.description: Observable pass/fail criteria; manual-qa consumes these directly as its checklist.

testing_strategy.description: How the feature will be tested (manual + automated).

product_intake.description: Normalized product discovery intake: what the request is, what is known, and what is not. Evidence-first — every claim carries a verified|assumption|unknown status with its source, and explicit 'unknown'/'TBD' is an allowed answer but must never be guessed. The intake is produced by a parallel consilium (product-analyst + product-researcher), so every content field is a MERGEABLE ARRAY: strict fan-in concatenates the slots' arrays deterministically, and a single scalar (problem_statement/context) would block on the first divergent phrasing between the two roles. Empty arrays are valid; 'unknown'/'TBD' string entries are the explicit way to represent missing knowledge.

problem_statements.description: The product problem or opportunity, one or two sentences per entry, from each intake role; 'TBD' allowed only when genuinely unknown and marked as such.

contexts.description: Business/product context per intake role; explicit 'unknown' entries allowed.

stakeholders.description: Stakeholders affected by or interested in the problem; 'unknown' allowed explicitly.

constraints.description: Constraints that bound any solution; 'unknown' allowed explicitly.

open_questions.description: Open questions that must be answered before the direction is decided; 'unknown' allowed explicitly.

status.description: verified = observed/confirmed from a source; assumption = unverified but stated as such; unknown = not known yet.

source.description: Where the claim came from (file:line, interview, doc, web source); 'n/a' for explicit assumptions/unknowns.

product_framing.description: Problem framing produced by the product analyst from the intake: restated problem, target users, success criteria and non-goals. Verified facts and assumptions stay distinct.

target_users.description: Who experiences the problem; 'unknown'/'TBD' allowed explicitly.

success_criteria.description: Observable product outcomes that would show the problem is solved.

non_goals.description: Explicitly out of scope for this discovery.

assumptions.description: Assumptions shaping the framing, each marked as an assumption (never dressed as a verified fact).

product_evidence.description: Evidence and alternatives gathered by the product researcher: verified facts, assumptions, unknowns, evidence gaps, and product alternatives considered. No fabricated data or invented sources.

status.description: verified = observed/confirmed; assumption = unverified but stated; unknown = not known yet.

source.description: Where the claim came from (file:line, doc, web source, interview); 'n/a' for explicit assumptions/unknowns.

gaps.description: Evidence gaps that must be validated before the direction can be considered solid.

product_critique.description: Adversarial review of the framing and evidence. The verdict is one of proceed|needs_more_validation|defer|reject and is never softened to be agreeable.

verdict.description: proceed = evidence supports moving to approval; needs_more_validation = direction plausible but evidence insufficient; defer = right area, not now; reject = the framing/direction itself is wrong or unsafe.

findings.description: Concrete critique points: unsupported claims, weak evidence, missing alternatives, framing errors.

blocking_gaps.description: Evidence or analysis gaps that must close before proceed.

product_spec.description: Synthesized product direction prepared by the product strategist from framing, evidence and critique. Product-level only — no APIs, no architecture, no implementation details. Every product-level concept is REQUIRED as its own field: an unknown/TBD concept is represented by an explicit array entry (e.g. 'unknown'/'TBD') or the string 'unknown', never by silently omitting the field — a spec that only carries recommendation/value/risk is not a decision.

recommendation.description: The strategist's recommendation to the product owner.

value_proposition.description: What is delivered, to whom, and why it matters; 'unknown' allowed explicitly.

opportunity.description: Size/attractiveness of the opportunity; 'unknown' allowed explicitly.

target_users.description: Who the direction is for; explicit 'unknown'/'TBD' entries allowed.

solution_direction.description: Product-level direction (what and why) — deliberately NOT an implementation plan; 'TBD' allowed explicitly.

success_metrics.description: Observable product outcomes that would show the direction works; explicit 'unknown'/'TBD' entries allowed.

guardrail_metrics.description: Metrics that must NOT regress (safety/constraints the direction may not trade away); explicit 'unknown'/'TBD' entries allowed.

scope.description: What the direction covers; explicit 'TBD' entries allowed.

anti_scope.description: Explicitly out of scope — the boundary that stops creep; explicit 'TBD' entries allowed.

risks.description: Risks that remain even after critique; explicit 'unknown' entries allowed.

validation_plan.description: What must be validated before/after implementation; empty when recommendation is proceed.

evidence_trace.description: Maps each recommendation claim to product_evidence items by verified|assumption|unknown status.

open_decisions.description: Product decisions still open for the owner; empty when none.

product_prd.description: Deterministic Markdown product PRD rendered by the engine from the five product-discovery source artifacts. Exact manifest fields — no extras, none missing. content is the rendered markdown; content_hash is sha256 of it and of the document file bytes; source_hash is the deterministic key-order-independent hash of the five source artifacts at render time (stale sources are detected by re-hashing).

path.description: Safe relative path of the markdown document inside the state dir.

source_artifacts.description: The five source artifact ids in fixed order.

source_hash.description: sha256 of the canonical serialization of the five source artifacts at render time.

content.description: The full rendered markdown; must equal the document file bytes.

product_approval_record.description: Durable record of the human product-owner approval. Interactive only — product approval is never auto-approved or inferred; the decision must be exactly one of proceed|needs_more_validation|defer|reject, recorded via workflow_checkpoint with checkpoint_kind=product_approval, authorization=human, and actor_provenance bound to the product-owner answer.

approved_by.description: Who approved — always a human product owner, never an autonomous agent.

product_handoff.description: Handoff of an approved product direction to the next workflow. next_workflow is 'spec-preparation' ONLY when decision == 'proceed'; for needs_more_validation | defer | reject it MUST be 'none' with a blocked_reason.

product_spec_artifact.description: Artifact id of the approved product spec (e.g. 'product_spec').

instructions.description: What the next workflow must spec and what evidence it must preserve.

blocked_reason.description: Why the direction was NOT handed off; required when decision != proceed.

dod.description: Definition of Done — acceptance criteria fixed BEFORE code, each with how it is verified and (when closed) the proof. Produced early (clarify/discovery/diagnose), then FANNED IN by later stages: every role with relevant context may APPEND items (with source + unique id) or CLOSE an existing item (pending→met with evidence). The dod_complete gate and the Stop backstop (hooks/dod-gate.sh) require every item met WITH evidence before a task may claim done.

id.description: Unique item id, convention `<source>-<n>` (e.g. architecture-1). Lets fan-in contributors append without colliding and lets closers reference a specific item.

source.description: Stage id that contributed this item (e.g. exploration, architecture, code_review, qa_tests, manual_qa). Defaults to the producing stage.

criterion.description: Concrete, observable acceptance criterion — not 'works' but what specifically must happen.

verify_method.description: How it is checked: a manual-qa scenario, a screenshot that must show X, a test, a curl.

evidence.description: Proof: gist URL, screenshot path + WHAT IS VISIBLE on it (input/output present? errors?), test output, curl result, root-cause statement. A bare checkbox is not proof.

contributions.description: Optional audit trail of the fan-in: keyed by contributing stage id. The interpreter/hooks never require it, but it makes the multi-source history inspectable.

closed.description: Item ids this stage moved pending→met.

by.description: Agent name(s) that made the contribution.

updated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the last append/close. Bumped on every fan-in write.

type_requirements_met.description: Confirms the per-type minimum items are present. Minimums: BUG_FIX → root cause named (not symptom) + repro-before reproduces + repro-after does not + affected scenario checked in manual-qa. FEATURE → each acceptance criterion mapped to a manual-qa step (both remote+docker modes if the feature touches agent/sessions). QA/report → published via publish-gist-report skill, screenshots actually visible (not broken). Any UI → DoD records what must be visible on the screenshot; on close, what is actually visible is written.

teams_hint.description: Team ids the CTO already considers relevant (optional, from scope analysis).

summary.description: Compact lead summary — raw artifacts stay in .work-state/artifacts/<team>/.

lecture_acquisition.description: Provider-neutral, bounded URL acquisition handoff. Persisted artifacts are schema version 2 and must carry an engine-issued feature/run/stage/intake binding.

lecture_intake.description: URL-first intake for lecture-research: extract exactly one public video/playlist URL plus the natural-language research prompt. The URL is the only source prerequisite; no user transcript, captions, or media file is requested. Produced by the intake (orchestrator) stage with acquisition-pending provenance.

task.description: The research question/goal the user asked about the lectures/playlist.

sources.description: Every lecture/playlist source the research may use. Each entry requires observable provenance so downstream evidence can be traced.

id.description: Stable source id (e.g. lecture-01) referenced by every downstream evidence field.

location.description: Where the source lives: file path, URL, or playlist id.

provenance.description: How/where the source was obtained (downloaded, provided file, linked in task) and any timecode/indexing available.

rights.description: Explicit rights declarations. Absence is fail-closed.

constraints.description: Boundaries from the request (language, scope, which lectures matter).

lecture_mapping.description: Bounded parallel mapping of normalized lecture_acquisition evidence. Mapping consumes the acquisition artifact and performs no network access or URL fetching. URL-derived units retain human-readable evidence and may carry structured evidence_refs for precise timestamped citations. Produced by the lecture_mapping (consilium) stage; the required 'lectures' array merges deterministically across slots (concat + JSON-identity dedupe), the required 'coverage' scalar resolves via the declared fan_in resolution.

coverage.description: What was mapped vs. what remains unknown across the assigned source slice (deterministic first-slot synthesis of the parallel contributions).

title.description: Short title of the mapped unit.

source_id.description: Intake source id this unit was mapped from.

evidence.description: Quoted transcript/source evidence with timecode where available — required, entries without evidence are rejected.

evidence_refs.description: Structured citations for URL-derived units. Each ref must point to a normalized acquisition evidence segment; timestamps are finite with end_seconds strictly greater than start_seconds. Existing human-readable evidence remains required for compatibility.

quote.description: Bounded quoted evidence retained alongside the readable evidence field.

end_seconds.description: Finite segment end in seconds; must be strictly greater than start_seconds.

uncertainty.description: What is unknown/ambiguous in this unit.

gaps.description: Sources or segments that could not be mapped, and why.

sources_consulted.description: Intake source ids actually mapped (mergeable by fan-in).

lecture_candidates.description: Synthesized, deduplicated candidate findings produced by the synthesis (single analyst) stage. Each candidate is grounded in quoted evidence sources and records its dedupe/conflict history.

topic.description: One synthesized finding: a deduped claim/insight grounded in the mapped lectures.

evidence_sources.description: Provenance: every claim is backed by these intake sources.

source_id.description: Intake source id providing this evidence.

evidence.description: Quoted evidence / timecode backing this candidate.

conflicts.description: Dedupe/conflict record: overlapping claims merged here, disagreements listed with the winning source and the losing sources — never discarded silently. Empty array when no conflicts arose.

relevance.description: Why this candidate matters for the intake task question.

deduped_count.description: Number of mapping units merged away during synthesis.

lecture_repo_fit.description: Read-only repo-fit plus security/IP review of the candidates. Produced by the repo_fit (consilium) stage; the required 'findings' array merges deterministically across slots. Verdict is an optional per-slot summary — the approval stage is the authoritative decision point.

findings.description: Repo-fit/security/IP findings, each grounded in observable evidence.

category.description: repo_fit = claim matches the codebase; mismatch = claim contradicts it; security/ip = review findings; gap = claim with no repo anchor.

evidence.description: Concrete observable evidence: quoted source evidence, commit hash, file path, symbol.

files.description: Repo file paths the finding cites.

verdict.description: Optional per-slot summary verdict; not a gate input.

unverified_claims.description: Candidate claims the repository neither supports nor refutes.

lecture_decision.description: Explicit human decision on the research findings, produced by the approval (orchestrator) stage. The approval gate completes for either an explicit 'approved' or 'rejected' verdict — both are terminal research outcomes and neither launches implementation. This workflow is research-only and never implements.

verdict.description: Explicit decision. Gate: approval stage completes on 'approved' or 'rejected' — both terminal, neither starts implementation.

rationale.description: Why approved/rejected (user words, or the documented autonomous decision).

approved_candidates.description: Candidate ids accepted for any follow-up.

next_steps.description: Notes for a future, separately-classified slice — never started by this workflow.

feature_workspace.description: Canonical FeatureWorkspace aggregate (specification/types.ts). Identity, path bindings, and phase records are additionally enforced by validateFeatureWorkspaceRecord.

feature_id.description: Immutable, branch-independent safe single path segment.

project_root_identity.description: Pinned filesystem identity for the authorized project root; path text alone is not authority.

specification_phase_version.description: Immutable content/provenance for one phase revision (specification/types.ts PhaseArtifactVersion). Versioned ids are never overwritten; replaced readable projections archive under history/.

dispatch_id.description: Proves which subagent dispatch produced the content.

source_artifact_hash.description: SHA-256 of canonical typed worker output.

semantic_model.description: Complete typed immutable semantic model; exact phase shape is enforced by the engine.

document_paths.description: All paths remain inside the feature workspace.

document_hashes.description: path to SHA-256; detects manual edits or materialization drift.

constitution_record.description: Exact constitution policy binding (specification/types.ts ConstitutionBinding); the version label is never trusted without content_sha256.

path.description: Project-relative policy path, realpath-bounded to the authorized project.

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact bytes used for validation or approval.

semantic_hash.description: SHA-256 of normalized policy sections; impact comparison only.

bound_at.description: Audit only; excluded from content hashes.

constitution_provider_selection.description: Immutable resolution result for the project policy location (explicit override, one discovered provider, or native default).

selection_hash.description: Binds provider id, path, template, configuration, discovery evidence.

constitution_gate_record.description: Durable constitution prerequisite record shared by native preparation and external intake (specification/types.ts ConstitutionGateRecord).

checkpoint_ref.description: Required only when a generated or corrected constitution is approved.

constitution_impact_assessment.description: Typed semantic-impact assessment over the bound artifact set (specification/types.ts ConstitutionImpactAssessment).

specification_validation.description: Machine-readable phase validation bound to one artifact version (specification/types.ts PhaseValidationResult); only pass permits awaiting_approval.

artifact_version.description: Must match the current artifact to authorize a checkpoint.

implementation_handoff.description: Frozen executor-neutral implementation contract (specification/types.ts ImplementationHandoff); the tasks array is the only canonical implementation task source.

content_provenance.description: Imported source provenance; content is data only and cannot authorize execution.

depends_on.description: No self-reference, dangling id, or cycle.

observable_behavior.description: Terminal conformance requires executed-test evidence when true.

constitution_binding.description: Exact constitution policy binding (constitution_record); the version label is never trusted without content_sha256.

open_decisions.description: Open blocking decisions must be empty when ready.

import_framework.description: Required for external handoffs; omitted for native handoffs.

import_mapping_id.description: Required for external handoffs; omitted for native handoffs.

import_mapping_version.description: Required for external handoffs; omitted for native handoffs.

import_selected_paths.description: Required for external handoffs; exact selected source projection.

import_ignored_candidates.description: Required for external handoffs; exact ignored source candidates.

import_intake_paths.description: Required for external handoffs; exact source-intake roots/paths used to discover the snapshot.

import_document_language.description: Required for external handoffs; exact captured document language.

import_document_language_source.description: Required for external handoffs; exact language provenance.

import_source_revision.description: Required for external handoffs; exact captured source revision.

import_limits.description: Exact normalized import ceilings bound to the persisted snapshot; omitted only for legacy artifacts.

execution_claim.description: Exclusive ownership of one ready handoff version, keyed by handoff digest (specification/types.ts ExecutionClaim).

import_snapshot.description: Immutable normalization of exact external sources; sources stay read-only (specification/types.ts ImportSnapshot).

source_revision.description: Git revision or null; per-file hashes remain authoritative.

normalized_content_ref.description: Typed artifact id; content is treated as data, not instructions.

limits.description: Exact normalized import ceilings; omitted only for legacy artifacts.

compatibility_supplement.description: Local, versioned supplement; never alters or impersonates external content (specification/types.ts CompatibilitySupplement).

closure_entry.description: One immutable requirement-closure matrix row (specification/types.ts RequirementClosureEntry); the closed row shape enforced for implementation_conformance.entries.

requirement_id.description: Self for a requirement row; owning requirement for an acceptance row.

observable_behavior.description: Copied from the frozen verification obligations, never inferred.

implementation_conformance.description: The executor-neutral requirement-closure matrix gating terminal feature completion (specification/types.ts ImplementationConformanceResult); executors can submit evidence but never add, remove, reinterpret, or waive rows.

matrix_digest.description: SHA-256; immutable, content-addressed, idempotent for the same inputs.

requirement_id.description: Self for a requirement row; owning requirement for an acceptance row.

observable_behavior.description: Copied from the frozen verification obligations, never inferred.

format_recognition.description: Advisory format recognition result; recognition never changes gates (specification/types.ts FormatRecognitionResult).

selected_paths.description: Immutable source-root-relative references only; no absolute paths, empty/dot/parent segments, or platform-separator ambiguity.

constitution_draft.description: Typed constitution draft worker output (T027); attributes the authoring dispatch and binds the exact constitution policy the draft was produced against (specification/types.ts ConstitutionGateRecord prerequisites).

gate_id.description: Stable identifier of the constitution gate record this draft belongs to.

feature_id.description: Immutable, branch-independent feature identity of the requesting workspace.

run_key.description: Explicit run key of the dispatching workflow run.

version.description: Immutable draft revision; draft versions are never overwritten.

document_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact document bytes.

worker.description: Attribution of the authoring worker dispatch; stable and audit-facing.

role.description: Declared profile role of the authoring worker.

agent.description: Registered agent type that authored the draft.

dispatch_id.description: Capability-bound dispatch id proving which dispatch produced the content.

constitution_binding.description: Exact constitution policy binding (constitution_record); the version label is never trusted without content_sha256.

specify_draft.description: Complete immutable semantic model for one readable Specify, Plan, or Tasks phase. Every readable projection is rendered from this model byte-for-byte.

plan_draft.description: Complete immutable semantic model for one readable Specify, Plan, or Tasks phase. Every readable projection is rendered from this model byte-for-byte.

task_graph.description: Complete immutable semantic model for one readable Specify, Plan, or Tasks phase. Every readable projection is rendered from this model byte-for-byte.

phase_validation.description: Readable and machine-readable phase validation bound to one artifact version (specification/types.ts PhaseValidationResult); only pass permits awaiting_approval, and a checkpoint is impossible before a current passing validation result exists.

artifact_version.description: Must match the current artifact version to authorize a checkpoint.

remediation.description: Actionable remediation; required when status is not pass.

blocking_findings.description: Pass/fail invariant: empty when status is pass and non-empty when status is fail.

constitution.description: Per-principle result plus the exact constitution binding used.

traceability_summary.description: Required after Plan and Tasks; null is only acceptable before upstream phases exist.

specification_phase_model.description: Complete immutable semantic model for one readable Specify, Plan, or Tasks phase. Every readable projection is rendered from this model byte-for-byte.

specification_status.description: Readable specification-status projection (T027) exposing phase status, approvals, and the typed next action for one feature run; regenerated from the durable FeatureWorkspace aggregate and never independently trusted.

run_key.description: Explicit run key of the generating workflow run.

constitution_binding.description: Exact constitution policy binding (constitution_record); null before the prerequisite is bound.

next_action.description: Typed next action using the canonical WorkspaceNextActionKind vocabulary; must identify a valid command, checkpoint, or remediation, or none.

command.description: Exact command, checkpoint id, or remediation entry point; null for checkpoint and none kinds.

updated_at.description: Audit only; the projection is regenerated from the durable aggregate.
